commentaryEvent.comment: The Bulldogs' intercept game has been the difference in the match, with the Dogs outscoring the Demons 10.6.66 to 3.5.23 from this source. They were exceptional from defensive half, outscoring Melbourne 10.5.65 to 1.4.10 from defensive half chains, their best return from defensive half this season.
The siren has sounded to end Q4.
After the highest rated game ever by a Bulldog last week, Ed Richards has been superb once again with 30 disposals, 14 contested possessions, eight clearances, 12 score involvements and a goal.

The stoppages could be Melbourne's road to a remarkable comeback win. They enjoy an advantage of 11 in clearance differential and have outscored the Bulldogs 8.10.58 to 4.5.29. This includes an advantage of 18 to seven in centre bounce clearances. It is seven to two in this quarter, with the Demons scoring from four of these seven centre bounce clearances.
Harrison Petty has now taken eight contested marks for the match, the most since Aaron Naughton took nine in 2019. The all-time record is 10 contested marks taken by Wayne Carey in 2000.
The Bulldogs have kicked the first three goals of the first, third and fourth quarters tonight.

Cooper Hynes now has the first two goals of the quarter for the Bulldogs to give them some breathing space. It was also the seventh goal the Bulldogs have scored from defensive half. Their total of 7.3.45 is their second-best return from defensive half scores for the season.

The Bulldogs get the opening goal of the final quarter, courtesy of a centre clearance. While they trial centre clearances six to 11, the Bulldogs have outscored Melbourne 2.0.12 to 1.2.8 from this source for the match.

Both captains have been influential for their respective sides. Marcus Bontempelli has 21 disposals, a match-high nine score involvements and a goal for the Bulldogs, while Max Gawn has 23 disposals, 11 contested possessions and eight clearances for the Demons.
The siren has sounded to end Q3.

Harrison Petty now has a career-high six contested marks today. He has been a significant presence for the Demons today with 12 disposals, eight marks, five score involvements and two goals in the absence of Jacob van Rooyen.
Demons Interchange - Matthew Jefferson and is possibly out for the game.
Bulldogs Interchange - Aaron Naughton and is possibly out for the game.

An outstanding goal to Caleb Windsor has roared Melbourne back into the contest. It was the Demons' 11th score from 32 clearances today, a strike rate of 34 per cent. Melbourne has scored from 29 per cent of their clearances this season, ranked fourth.
Melbourne kicks its first goal of the match from a defensive half chain. The Demons have been outscored 6.2.38 to 1.3.9 from defensive half chains today.

The Bulldogs lead post-clearance contested possession this quarter 13 to four. This is a great outcome for the Bulldogs who are only ranked 15th for post-clearance contested possession for the season.
Four of the five Western Bulldogs goals from defensive 50 have come via intercepts. This is their best return from defensive 50 intercepts since Round 20, 2025.

Tom Sparrow recorded the first three clearances of the quarter for Melbourne, who also registered the first three inside 50s of the term, but it is a goal from a clearance to Rhylee West of the Bulldogs that opens up the major scoring of the all-important third term.
The Bulldogs lead the scores from intercept battle 5.3.33 to 2.2.14 today and have already scored 4.1.25 from defensive 50 chains, their third-best return of the season.
The siren has sounded to end Q2.

Harrison Petty looks the most likely forward for Melbourne today. He has four contested marks, four marks inside 50 and two goals. It is already a season-best contested mark tally for Petty and one off his career-high of five, taken in 2024.
There has been a high number of stoppages in the second quarter, 33 in total, but 16 of these stoppages have resulted in another stoppage. Melbourne lead the clearances nine to eight this term.

Melbourne leads the contested possession count by nine in the second quarter, which has propelled them to advantage of six in inside 50s. The ball has lived in the Demons half in the second term, with Melbourne enjoying 68 per cent time in forward half.

Both sides have increased their pressure in the second quarter. The Western Bulldogs lead the tackle count by three this term, but the Demons lead the overall pressure rating for the quarter 196 to 187.

Max Gawn has recorded 24 hitouts so far in this match, compared to the entire Western Bulldogs team that has just five. Despite the advantage, the first possessions are 13 apiece in the 36 ruck contests that Gawn has attended and the Bulldogs lead the clearances by three.
The Bulldogs have already kicked 3.1.19 from defensive 50 chains today, their best return since Round 12 this season. It is also already their fifth best return this season from defensive 50 chains.
Melbourne leads the inside 50 count by five at quarter time, but the Bulldogs have bounced out of the Melbourne forward half well, outscoring the Demons 3.1.19 to 0.1.1 from defensive half chains.
The siren has sounded to end Q1.
Demons Interchange - Jake Lever off due to an injury.
Both sides have 12 inside 50s for the match, but the Bulldogs have generated a score from 75 per cent of their entries, compared to 33 per cent from Melbourne.
Bulldogs Interchange - Bailey Williams off due to an injury.
Melbourne lead the clearances eight to three and have outscored the Bulldogs 1.1.7 to 0.1.1 from this source. The Demons rank fifth this season for scores from stoppage, averaging 39 points per game.

Melbourne gets themselves on the board with their first goal of the match through Ed Langdon, but their ball use has been patchy to start the game, kicking at an efficiency of just 54 per cent, compared to the Bulldogs' 71 per cent.

It is now three goals from three inside 50s for the Bulldogs, who have kicked two of their three goals from defensive 50 chains. They average just 13 points per game from defensive 50 chains, ranked 15th in the AFL.
The Bulldogs have started well with two goals from their first two inside 50s of the match. The first goal was courtesy of a forward half intercept, while the second goal came via a kick-in chain.
Demons Interchange - Daniel Turner off due to an injury.

Melbourne had 28 more intercepts than Port Adelaide last week, the second-largest differential ever in a match. From these intercepts, the Demons scored 111 points, the most by any team this year and their most in any game on record.
The Bulldogs are involved in the lowest scoring games of any team this season, with an average of 157.3 points in their matches.

Ins for Bulldogs: C.Budarick, B.Dale, M.Bontempelli, R.Gardner
